summary: Follow-up to MPI-484 on the users instruction to leave no loose strings: build the cross-instance restart channel. Filed as 486 after an id COLLISION - I took 485 from next_id while a peer was committing their own MPI-485 (aa60dadf, the orphan Pod sweep card) and my write overwrote their brief/task/events on disk. Theirs was restored from HEAD intact and mine re-filed here. NOTE: the code was written before this card existed; the card-then-edit ordering was not followed, because the work continued directly from the 484 close-out conversation.

doing -> done (complete). Cross-instance restart channel shipped: a non-owner /comfy/start with isUserRestart writes .engine-restart-request.json in the shared repo-scoped ENGINE_ROOT and answers delegated:true; the owner runs a 2s watcher armed on spawn and cleared on exit that deletes the request BEFORE restarting and ignores any request older than its own spawn - both orderings pinned by tests because each failure is an infinite restart loop. Broker rejected: best-effort, and one appId cannot address one instance. VERIFIED LIVE: plain attach writes no file, isUserRestart returns delegated:true with a well-formed record, owner engine on 48188 untouched. NOT verified live: the honouring half - it needs an instance that OWNS an engine and the users app held 48188 all session; 11/11 tests and the ordering assertions stand in, and one end-to-end run is owed when the port is free. Also fixed a dead pointer this created: rule 8 referenced a section that did not exist until the Cross-instance engine restart section was written.
Archived out of board.columns.done to .agents/mpi-kanban/tasks/_archived/MPI-486/ (workspace preserved intact). mpi-archive run 2026-08-21.
